articles.title: “Who Earns ₹9,000 Today?”: Supreme Court Questions Husband’s Income Claim in Alimony Dispute
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: The Supreme Court of India on Friday witnessed a sharp exchange during the hearing of a matrimonial dispute, as it questioned a husband’s claim that he earned only ₹9,000 per month and was unable to pay higher alimony.

body.html:
The Supreme Court of India on Friday witnessed a sharp exchange during the hearing of a matrimonial dispute, as it questioned a husband’s claim that he earned only ₹9,000 per month and was unable to pay higher alimony.

A Bench comprising Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta said the income claim was “difficult to swallow”.

“Who earns ₹9,000 these days?” Justice Nath remarked.

When Advocate George Pothan, appearing for the husband, submitted that his client earned ₹325 per day, the Court expressed scepticism and said it could summon the employer for clarification. Justice Nath even remarked in lighter vein that the counsel could contribute towards the maintenance.

The matter relates to a petition filed by the wife seeking enhancement of alimony. A trial court had earlier awarded ₹6 lakh as full and final settlement, which the husband paid. Dissatisfied, the wife approached the High Court seeking ₹30 lakh, but her plea was rejected. She then moved the Supreme Court.

During the hearing, the wife’s counsel submitted two proposals: ₹12,000 per month for life with annual increments, or a lump sum payment of ₹30 lakh.

Pothan argued that alimony must be determined based on the husband’s financial capacity and liabilities. He stated that the husband was being supported by siblings and was bearing children’s education expenses. He further claimed that even the earlier alimony payment was made after the husband’s father sold joint family property.

Justice Mehta responded bluntly, stating, “Beg, borrow, steal — that is the principle. To maintain your wife.”

When the counsel reiterated that his client worked seven days a week earning ₹325 daily, the Bench indicated it might summon “Hindustan Auto Agency,” the employer, and seek an enquiry from the concerned authority.

Pothan submitted that colleagues were willing to file affidavits confirming similar wages and that the employer could also file an affidavit.

At one stage, Justice Mehta suggested reconciliation, saying the husband could keep the wife with him as “the best way out.” The counsel responded that the wife had filed complaints against the husband’s parents, casting doubt on reconciliation.

The Court has reserved its order in the matter.

articles.title: 6-Year-Old Found Locked in School Bus for 7 Hours in Noida; Parents Allege Serious Lapses
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A six-year-old UKG student of Amity International School was found locked inside a school bus for nearly seven hours after reportedly falling asleep during his morning commute on February 26. The incident occurred in Noida.

body.html:
A six-year-old UKG student of Amity International School was found locked inside a school bus for nearly seven hours after reportedly falling asleep during his morning commute on February 26.

The incident occurred in Noida. According to information, the child boarded the bus from his housing society in the morning but fell asleep during the journey. En route, the bus reportedly developed a mechanical fault, and other students were shifted to a relief vehicle.

Amid the vehicle change, the sleeping child was allegedly overlooked by the driver and the attendant. The original bus was later driven to a parking yard in Sector 81, around 25 kilometres away from the school campus, with the child still inside.

The boy’s parents became anxious when he did not return home in the afternoon. After contacting the school and initiating a search, the father located his son inside the locked bus at the yard.

The child was found frightened, sweating and crying. Though physically unharmed, the incident has raised concerns about his psychological well-being.

Parents have alleged discrepancies in attendance records, claiming the child was marked present in the bus register but absent in the classroom attendance. They stated that no alert was sent regarding his absence from class.

Principal Renu Singh said the school has taken serious note of the incident and initiated a comprehensive review of its transport protocols. She assured that strict action would be taken against those responsible.

Local police have been informed, though no formal written complaint had been filed by the family at the time of reporting.

articles.title: 6-Month-Old Dies After ‘Expired Injection’ at Hyderabad Hospital; Mob Storms Facility
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A six-month-old infant allegedly died after being administered expired medicine at a private hospital in Hyderabad, triggering unrest and vandalism at the facility. The incident occurred on February 21 at Crayons Hospital in Bandlaguda Jagir.

body.html:
A six-month-old infant allegedly died after being administered expired medicine at a private hospital in Hyderabad, triggering unrest and vandalism at the facility.

The incident occurred on February 21 at Crayons Hospital in Bandlaguda Jagir. The infant, identified as Ramu, had been taken to the hospital by his parents for persistent fever. According to K. Raghavender, Sub-Inspector at Rajendranagar Police Station, the child had previously received treatment at the same hospital and had recovered.

The parents alleged that the infant was administered an Adrenaline Bitartrate injection that had expired on January 19, 2026. They produced photographs of a strip containing four vials, two of which were reportedly used. Medical experts stated that the injection is generally administered in critical emergencies to stimulate heart rate.

Hospital authorities, however, denied the allegation, stating that medicines administered during treatment are not handed over to attendants. Police said that multiple individuals had entered the hospital premises following the child’s death, making verification complex.

The infant, born several years after his two sisters, was declared dead despite emergency intervention. Following the announcement, a group of attendants and locals allegedly stormed the hospital, attacking staff including the Duty Medical Officer, nurses and supervisory personnel. Significant damage was reportedly caused to computers, an ultrasound machine, televisions and glass fixtures, disrupting medical services and creating panic among patients.

A written complaint has been filed by Dr. Abhishek M., Chief Pediatrician at the hospital. Allegations have also surfaced regarding police inaction during the violence.

An FIR has been registered against the treating doctor under Section 106(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, which pertains to causing death by rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide and carries a punishment of up to five years’ imprisonment and fine.

Police said the exact cause of death will be determined after the post-mortem and Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) reports. Further investigation is underway.

articles.title: Love Turns Violent in Bidadi: Woman Stabs Gym Trainer Boyfriend Over Marriage Refusal
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: In a shocking reversal of typical assault cases linked to failed relationships, a 30-year-old woman allegedly stabbed her boyfriend after he reportedly avoided her and refused to marry her. The incident occurred in Bidadi in Ramanagara taluk of Bengaluru South district.

body.html:
In a shocking reversal of typical assault cases linked to failed relationships, a 30-year-old woman allegedly stabbed her boyfriend after he reportedly avoided her and refused to marry her.

The incident occurred in Bidadi in Ramanagara taluk of Bengaluru South district. The injured man has been hospitalised in serious condition, while the accused woman has been taken into police custody.

According to police, Sudha (30) allegedly attacked her boyfriend Venugopal (27), a gym trainer working in Bidadi. Sudha was employed at a private company. The two reportedly met at a gym and had been in a relationship for about a year despite their age difference.

Police said Sudha frequently visited Venugopal’s residence. However, over the past four months, he had allegedly been avoiding her and refused to marry her. She also suspected him of having an affair with another woman.

Investigators said that for the past month, Venugopal had allegedly been evading her calls and making excuses to avoid meeting her. Sudha had reportedly been carrying a knife in her bag for the past week.

On the day of the incident, she allegedly called Venugopal out of his house in the evening, saying she wanted to talk. After a brief conversation, she allegedly stabbed him in the chest, stomach and arm before fleeing the scene.

Venugopal, bleeding profusely, managed to call his family and friends. He was rushed to a nearby hospital, where his condition remains critical.

A case has been registered at the Bidadi Police Station, and the accused is being questioned. Further investigation is underway.

articles.title: Bride Walks Out Mid-Ritual in Sringeri After Shocking Letter Exposes Groom’s Alleged Secrets
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A wedding in Sringeri town of Chikkamagaluru district was abruptly called off on Friday after the bride walked out of the mandap during the ceremony, alleging that the groom had concealed serious information.

body.html:
A wedding in Sringeri town of Chikkamagaluru district was abruptly called off on Friday after the bride walked out of the mandap during the ceremony, alleging that the groom had concealed serious information.

The marriage of 41-year-old Dikshit Hegde and 29-year-old Sushma was scheduled at Idiga Samudaya Bhavana in Sringeri. While this was Dikshit’s first marriage, Sushma had been married earlier and has a nine-year-old son. Family members and guests had gathered, and rituals were underway when the situation took a dramatic turn.

During the function, Sushma reportedly received a five-page anonymous complaint letter containing allegations about the groom that she claimed had never been disclosed. When she questioned the groom’s family, they allegedly asked her to complete the wedding first and discuss the matter later.

According to Sushma, the groom had misrepresented his age and had multiple police cases pending against him. She further alleged that he is an accused in a 2021 case involving the alleged rape of a minor and had not informed her about his mother’s health condition. She claimed that whenever she sought clarification earlier, he had deferred explanations until after the wedding.

As tensions escalated, officials from the Child Development Project Office and personnel from the Sringeri Police Station arrived at the venue and attempted mediation. However, Sushma refused to proceed, stating she could not begin married life on the basis of broken trust.

The wedding was formally called off, and the groom’s family left the venue. Police confirmed that a case has been registered and further action will be taken following investigation.

articles.title: 18 Killed in Devastating Fireworks Factory Blast in Andhra Pradesh; Bodies Flung into Fields
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: At least 18 persons were killed in a massive explosion at a fireworks manufacturing unit in Vetlapalem village of Samarlakota mandal in Kakinada district on Saturday afternoon.

body.html:
At least 18 persons were killed in a massive explosion at a fireworks manufacturing unit in Vetlapalem village of Samarlakota mandal in Kakinada district on Saturday afternoon.

The blast occurred around 2:00 PM at the Suryashree Fire Works unit and was reportedly heard up to five kilometres away. The impact was so powerful that bodies were flung into nearby paddy fields and cracks developed in the roof of a nearby school building.

Vangalapudi Anitha confirmed that at least 18 people have died, though some reports suggest the toll could rise to 19 or 20. Most of the deceased are believed to be women workers who were inside the unit at the time of the explosion.

At least six persons sustained critical burn injuries ranging between 90% and 100% and are undergoing treatment at the Kakinada Government General Hospital.

Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu expressed deep grief over the tragedy and directed the Home Minister to rush to the spot to oversee rescue operations and ensure proper medical care for the injured.

Rescue and relief operations are ongoing, and officials are assessing the extent of damage.

articles.title: Instagram Trap in Kochi: Disabled Man Assaulted, Stripped and Filmed in Hotel Room; 4 Arrested
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: The Kadavanthra Police Station have arrested four persons, including a woman, in connection with the brutal assault and attempted extortion of a hearing- and speech-impaired man in Panampilly Nagar.

body.html:
The Kadavanthra Police Station have arrested four persons, including a woman, in connection with the brutal assault and attempted extortion of a hearing- and speech-impaired man in Panampilly Nagar.

The arrested accused are Safna of North Paravur, John Rahul of Vyttila, Amal of Irumpanam and Anand of Maradu. A fifth accused, Sanju of Kochi, remains absconding and a manhunt has been launched to trace him.

The victim, a 30-year-old native of Nallila in Kollam, is undergoing treatment for spinal injuries. Due to his hearing and speech impairment, police recorded his statement with the assistance of a sign language expert. He lodged the complaint on February 24.

According to police, the prime accused Safna befriended the victim through Instagram and developed a rapport through chats. Though the victim initially suggested meeting at a beach, she allegedly invited him to a hotel near the South Bridge in Panampilly Nagar on February 22.

Investigators said the gang had meticulously planned the trap. When the victim reached the hotel around 6.30 pm, some accused were already hiding inside the room, including in the bathroom, while others arrived shortly thereafter.

Police stated that the group’s motive was financial. The gang allegedly intended to film the victim in compromising positions to blackmail him. When he refused to strip and engage in sexual acts, he was forcibly disrobed and assaulted. He was repeatedly punched and kicked, and one accused struck his hand with a heavy torch while attempting to hit his head. The victim blocked the blow, sustaining injuries.

The accused also allegedly accessed his Google Pay account to transfer money but found insufficient funds. Nude photographs were reportedly taken before the victim managed to escape. Police have seized the accused persons’ mobile phones and are attempting to recover deleted data.

John and Anand were apprehended late Tuesday night, while Safna and another accomplice were traced to an apartment in Kakkanad early Wednesday morning. All accused were identified through CCTV visuals and call records.

The accused have been booked under multiple sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) relating to assault, criminal intimidation and extortion, along with Section 92(a) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act for atrocities against persons with disabilities. They will be produced before the court for remand.

Police said the investigation is ongoing, including examination of digital evidence and medical reports.

articles.title: Fuel Theft Horror on NH-91: Thar Drags Bike for 7 KM, CCTV Captures Shocking Fire Chase in GN
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A 22-year-old driver was detained in Greater Noida after allegedly attempting to flee a petrol pump without paying, triggering a dramatic chase that ended with a motorcycle being dragged for several kilometres on a highway, police said.

body.html:
A 22-year-old driver was detained in Greater Noida after allegedly attempting to flee a petrol pump without paying, triggering a dramatic chase that ended with a motorcycle being dragged for several kilometres on a highway, police said.

The incident occurred on Friday evening at a fuel station in the Dhum Manikpur area. The accused, identified as Harsh from Sikandrabad, reportedly filled diesel in his black Mahindra Thar. When asked to make the payment, he claimed he would transfer the amount online but allegedly sped away without completing the transaction.

Petrol pump employee Kuldeep Sharma chased the SUV on a motorcycle along GT Road and onto National Highway 91. During the pursuit, the Thar collided with Sharma’s motorcycle, which became lodged in the front of the SUV. The vehicle allegedly dragged the entangled bike for nearly 5 to 7 kilometres.

CCTV footage captured the sequence, showing the motorcycle catching fire while being dragged, with flames visible during the chase. Acting on alerts, police intercepted the SUV near the Luharli toll plaza and took the driver into custody.

The Thar has been seized for forensic examination. Sharma sustained injuries in the incident and is undergoing medical treatment.

Police termed the matter a serious case involving attempted fuel theft, rash and negligent driving, endangerment of life, and possible additional charges related to the fire and injuries. Legal proceedings against the accused are underway.

articles.title: HATHRAS: Newlywed Bride Attacks Husband with Knife, Flees with Gold & Cash
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A case of alleged post-wedding theft has been reported from Hathras, where a newlywed bride is accused of attacking her husband and fleeing with jewellery and cash. According to the complaint filed by Sunil Kumar, the marriage took place on February 21, 2026.

body.html:
A case of alleged post-wedding theft has been reported from Hathras, where a newlywed bride is accused of attacking her husband and fleeing with jewellery and cash.

According to the complaint filed by Sunil Kumar, the marriage took place on February 21, 2026. Two days later, on February 23, the bride allegedly attacked him with a knife. He managed to escape unhurt. After the incident, she reportedly reassured him that she was willing to continue the marriage and stay with him.

However, on the night of February 25, she prepared dinner for Sunil but did not eat herself. After he fell asleep, she allegedly fled the house. The next morning, Sunil discovered she was missing.

The complainant has alleged that the bride took gold and silver jewellery, including a hansuli (necklace), pendant, maang tika, two gold rings and anklets, along with ₹18,000 in cash.

A formal complaint has been lodged at Kotwali Sadar Police Station. Police have initiated an investigation into charges of assault and theft.

The case has drawn comparisons with a June 2025 incident in Prayagraj, where a bride named Sitara allegedly threatened her groom with a knife on their wedding night before eloping with a partner. Authorities said further inquiry is underway.

articles.title: CCTV Shows Fatal Crash in Bilaspur: 4 Dead After Trailer Jumps Divider and Hits Scorpio Head-On
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Four persons were killed and one sustained critical injuries after a trailer rammed into a Scorpio SUV on the Raipur–Ratanpur Highway near Bilaspur, Chhattisgarh, in the early hours of Friday. The accident occurred around 2 am near Sambalpuri village under Sakri police station limits.

body.html:
Four persons were killed and one sustained critical injuries after a trailer rammed into a Scorpio SUV on the Raipur–Ratanpur Highway near Bilaspur, Chhattisgarh, in the early hours of Friday.

The accident occurred around 2 am near Sambalpuri village under Sakri police station limits. According to police, the trailer, heading towards Raipur, lost control, crossed the median and entered the opposite lane, colliding head-on with the Scorpio.

CCTV footage from a nearby dhaba shows several heavy vehicles parked along the roadside. A pickup truck was stationed on the left lane with hazard lights on. A dumper reportedly moved between the parked pickup and a long trailer. In an attempt to avoid the dumper, the trailer driver swerved, lost control and crashed into the oncoming SUV. Police said the Scorpio driver had less than two seconds to react.

The impact was severe. After hitting the Scorpio, the trailer struck another parked trailer and overturned. The SUV was completely mangled, trapping all five occupants. Rescue teams used a gas cutter in a two-hour operation to extricate the victims.

The deceased were identified as Chhatrapal Ratre (37), Vishal Lahre (25), Anmol Lahre (14) and Sonu Miri (28). The injured, Prakash Ratre, is undergoing treatment at Chhattisgarh Institute of Medical Sciences. The victims were returning home after attending a 25th wedding anniversary celebration at a nearby dhaba.

The trailer driver has been arrested and a case registered. Police are probing the role of roadside parking, heavy vehicle movement and driver negligence in the crash.
